It remeasured across all fourteen contracts -- 8 of 101 root required entries isolated by a negative fixture, eight contracts isolating none -- and, rather than land 101 fixtures that can rot the same way, asserts the property generatively: test-kits/contracts/catalog-registry.test.mjs drops each declared root required key from a valid example and requires the schema to reject it by name, with a floor of 101 keys exercised so a key cannot leave a required list quietly. What remains is narrower: that guard reads schema.required at the ROOT and nowhere else. A required list nested inside a subschema is outside it, and is defended only where test-kits/contracts/schema-mutation-coverage.test.mjs names one by hand -- ctr-ntf-001 deep_link.required is the single nested entry -- so nested requiredness across the catalog is still unmeasured.

The ENFORCEMENT half of FP-002 — that a narrower scope cannot override a live platform kill switch — cannot be expressed in a single decision document and is not materialized. It needs an evaluator that does not exist. The ORDER half is now enforced.

MR-002 duplicate-capability resolution and MR-003 circular-dependency blocking are registry properties across multiple manifests, and FP-003 stable allocation is an evaluator property over repeated inputs. Declared in untestable_by_fixture and NOT claimed as materialized.

The dependency range grammar (MR-003), the drain and shutdown protocol timing (MR-005), the bucket allocation algorithm (FP-003), the circuit-state machine (FP-004) and the admin APIs (MR-006, FP-006) are deliberately not inferred and remain open before freeze.

This said the package depends on WP-0A-CON-002 and WP-0A-A0-002, both unmerged. Both reached main long ago -- A0-002 at 41e47bf (PR #3) and CON-002 at 1eb31c2 (PR #4) -- as did the other two declared dependencies, WP-0A-A0-001 and WP-0A-CON-001, and this package now sits on top of all four.
